enhanced_information: Urea is produced in the liver as a waste product of protein metabolism, then transported to the kidneys for excretion. It is not degraded to ammonium in the urea cycle. Urea is a polar molecule due to the presence of the amino group and is derived from ammonia and carbon dioxide in the liver. It contains one carbonyl group and one amino group, not two ketone groups. Relevant evidence supports urea's interaction with enzymes in the liver and its presence in liver cells.
analysis: Urea is a waste product formed in the liver from ammonia resulting from protein metabolism. It is then transported to the kidneys for excretion, not the liver. Urea is not degraded to ammonium in the urea cycle; rather, it is the end product of the urea cycle. Urea is a polar molecule, not apolar, and does not easily form crystals. Urea is not obtained from arginine; it is synthesized in the liver. Urea has one ketone group and two amino groups, not two ketone groups and one amino group.
